sth_fishhall.text: Spider crabs, lobsters, mussels, and a conger that's been eyeing me up since Tuesday. The Fish Hall's at this end, the flowers and potatoes are at the other.
Jersey gets some of the biggest tides in Europe. When the sea goes out you can walk a mile on the sand, and I can pick up dinner for a quid.

then.text: Royals! Look at them. Scrape, don't peel, boil with a sprig of mint, butter and nothing else. Mèrcie, my friend, you've saved my season.
Jersey Royals are grown on steep south-facing fields called côtils, and dug by hand from April. First crop of the year, and half the island lines up for them.
Are those them? Oh, look at the skins. You can rub them off with your thumb. Wonderful. Here, you deserve something for the trouble.
And take this little one. It turned up in the bean crock aisle and I think it's yours.

else.text: Any luck with the Royals? Le Brocq's farm is up the lane north of town. They want a Vraicling's seaweed for the fields and a good fight from the old man first. Jersey hospitality.
Bouônjour. The stall's empty, and it's the Royal season, and I've nothing to sell. The man who usually supplies me is laid up. Could you fetch me a crop of Royals?
Try Le Brocq's farm, up the lane to the north of town. They'll want the right fertiliser and a bit of a show. Old Josué doesn't give his potatoes to anybody.
